slides.headline: The day before the Constitution was adopted, its own architect warned the country not to trust it blindly.
On November 25, 1949, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar delivered his closing speech to the Constituent Assembly, a day before the Constitution was formally adopted.
slides.body: In the speech, Ambedkar warned that a good constitution alone couldn't guarantee good governance - if things went wrong, he said, it wouldn't be because the Constitution was bad, but because the people entrusted to run it failed to live up to it.

slides.headline: He placed the responsibility on citizens and institutions, not just on the document itself.
slides.body: Ambedkar's closing argument was that a constitution is only as good as the people who operate it - a caution aimed at every future generation, not just the one adopting it the next day.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is still the responsibility Ambedkar described - a document that works only if the people running it choose to make it work.
slides.body: Nearly 80 years later, that warning is still the standard the country is measured against, not just the text of the Constitution itself.

sources.text: Supreme Court of India - Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Closing Speech, 25 Nov 1949
